facts.text: Falmouth earned its name when the Massachusetts Bay Colony renamed the area after the 1645 Parliamentary victory at the Battle of Falmouth in England.
The town’s earliest landmark was Fort Casco, a palisaded fort and trading post erected in 1698 after King William’s War.
Author Stephen King set several of his early short stories, including “Jerusalem’s Lot,” in the rural backdrop of Falmouth.
Before European settlement, the Abenaki‑Pennacook people called the area Aucocisco, living along the Presumpscot River and harvesting corn, beans, and squash.
English colonists abandoned Casco Bay twice—first in 1676 and again in 1690—after pressure from French and Indian attacks.
